## Merging ADNI Data

```{r}
#| label: load-packages



library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)


```

```{r, warning=FALSE}
#| label: read-data
somascanraw <- read_csv("protein_raw_data/CruchagaLab_CSF_SOMAscan7k_Protein_matrix_postQC_20230620.csv")
f01_duke_uplcraw <- read_excel("lifestyle_raw_data/f01_duke_uplc.xlsx")
f04_npiraw <- read_excel("lifestyle_raw_data/f04_npi.xlsx")
f06_medhistraw <- read_excel("lifestyle_raw_data/f06_medhist.xlsx")
lifestyle_dictionaryraw <- read_excel("lifestyle_raw_data/lifestyle_dictionary.xlsx")



```

```{r}
#| label: select-respective-variables

f01_duke_uplc <- f01_duke_uplcraw |>
  select(RID, DHA, EPA, HCys, VISCODE2, EXAMDATE) |>
  arrange(EXAMDATE, .by_group = TRUE) |>  
  group_by(RID) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>  
  ungroup()


f04_npi <- f04_npiraw |>
  select(RID, NPIK, NPIKTOT, VISCODE2, EXAMDATE) |>
  arrange(EXAMDATE, .by_group = TRUE) |>  
  group_by(RID) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>  
  ungroup()
 


f06_medhist <- f06_medhistraw |>
  select(RID, MH14ALCH,MH16SMOK, VISCODE2, VISDATE) |>
  arrange(VISDATE, .by_group = TRUE) |>  
  group_by(RID) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>  
  ungroup()




```

```{r}
#| label: merge-lifestyle

datasets <- list(
  f01_duke_uplc,
  f04_npi,
  f06_medhist
)

# Convert all RID variables to the same type
datasets <- lapply(datasets, function(x) {
  x |>
    mutate(RID = as.double(RID))
})



lifestyle_sa <- reduce(datasets, full_join, by = "RID") |>
  select(RID, DHA, EPA, HCys, NPIK, NPIKTOT, MH14ALCH, MH16SMOK, VISDATE, VISCODE2, EXAMDATE.x, EXAMDATE.y) |>
  mutate(
    EXAMDATE.y = as.numeric(EXAMDATE.y), as.Date(EXAMDATE.y, origin = "1899-12-30"),
    EXAMDATE.x = as.character(EXAMDATE.x),
    EXAMDATE.y = as.character(EXAMDATE.y),
    VISDATE = as.character(VISDATE),
    examdate = coalesce(EXAMDATE.x, EXAMDATE.y, VISDATE))




write.csv(lifestyle_sa, "lifestyle-sa.csv", row.names = FALSE)



```


```{r}
#| label: create-age-variable

# Read the Excel file (assuming the first row contains column names)
ptdemo <- read_excel("PTDEMOG_excel.xlsx")

# Set first row as column names and remove it
colnames(ptdemo) <- ptdemo[1, ]

ptdemo <- ptdemo |>
  slice(-1) |>
  select(RID, VISCODE2, PTGENDER, PTDOB) |>
  mutate(RID = as.double(RID))

lifestyle_demo <- ptdemo |>
  full_join(lifestyle_sa, by = "RID")


lifestyle_demo <- lifestyle_demo |>
  mutate(
    PTDOB = ymd(PTDOB),       
    examdate = ymd(examdate),
    age = as.numeric((examdate - PTDOB) / 365.25)
  )



```

```{r, error = TRUE}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# =============================================
# Step 1: Prepare the data
# =============================================

# Ensure ptau217_csf is numeric and filter NAs
lifestyle_7var_ptau <- lifestyle_7var_ptau %>%
  mutate(
    ptau217_csf = as.numeric(ptau217_csf)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ptau217_csf) & !is.na(age_at_csf_ptau) & !is.na(dx_entry))

# Define minimum valid pairs for LOESS
MIN_VALID_PAIRS <- 10  # Adjust as needed
LOESS_SPAN <- 0.5      # Smoothness parameter

# =============================================
# Step 2: Fit LOESS curves per disease group
# =============================================

loess_fits <- lifestyle_7var_ptau %>%
  group_by(dx_entry) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    # Extract data for the current group
    group_data <- .x
    age_vals <- group_data$age_at_csf_ptau
    ptau_vals <- group_data$ptau217_csf
    
    # Check for valid pairs
    valid_idx <- !is.na(age_vals) & !is.na(ptau_vals)
    n_valid <- sum(valid_idx)
    
    if (n_valid < MIN_VALID_PAIRS) {
      message(sprintf("Skipping %s: Only %d valid pairs (minimum %d required).",
                      first(group_data$dx_entry), n_valid, MIN_VALID_PAIRS))
      return(tibble::tibble())  # Return empty tibble
    }
    
    # Fit LOESS to the current group
    loess_fit <- tryCatch(
      loess(ptau_vals[valid_idx] ~ age_vals[valid_idx], span = LOESS_SPAN, degree = 1),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    
    if (is.null(loess_fit)) {
      message(sprintf("LOESS fitting failed for %s. Skipping.", first(group_data$dx_entry)))
      return(tibble::tibble())
    }
    
    # Generate 100 evenly spaced age values for predictions
    age_seq <- seq(min(age_vals, na.rm = TRUE),
                   max(age_vals, na.rm = TRUE),
                   length.out = 100)
    
    # Predict LOESS values
    fitted_vals <- predict(loess_fit, newdata = data.frame(age_at_csf_ptau = age_seq))
    
    # Ensure fitted_vals has 100 rows
    if (length(fitted_vals) != 100) {
      stop("Prediction failed: fitted_vals does not have 100 rows.")
    }

    # Create a data frame for the current group
    tibble::tibble(
      dx_entry = first(group_data$dx_entry),  # Single value (e.g., "AD")
      age = age_seq,                           # 100 values
      fitted = fitted_vals                     # 100 values
    )
  }) %>%
  filter(n() > 0)  # Remove empty groups

# =============================================
# Step 3: Plot the LOESS curves
# =============================================

# Check if there are any groups left to plot
if (nrow(loess_fits) == 0) {
  stop("No groups had sufficient data for LOESS fitting. Check your dataset.")
}

# Create the plot
ggplot(lifestyle_7var_ptau, aes(x = age_at_csf_ptau, y = ptau217_csf, color = dx_entry)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5) +  # Raw data points
  geom_line(
    data = loess_fits,
    aes(x = age, y = fitted, group = dx_entry, color = dx_entry),
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +  # LOESS curves
  labs(
    title = "PTAU217 CSF Levels by Disease Stage (LOESS Smoothing)",
    x = "Age at CSF PTAU Measurement",
    y = "PTAU217 CSF Levels",
    color = "Disease Stage"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

```
